messages:
maria: Quick Q — we're planning to remove the unpinned default and also add a new top-level `meta` field in responses. Are those two changes going to ship together? need to coordinate client SDKs and partner teams.

alex: We should avoid coupling them. Plan A: change pin semantics (allow customers to pin explicit model versions / remove implicit default) first. Plan B: roll out response envelope change via opt-in header so clients can migrate on their schedule.

jordan: Product ask: can we give a clear deprecation timeline that customers can rely on? suggested timeline: announce -> 90d soft-deprecation (warnings) -> 30d hard enforcement. Also need migration doc + SDK bumps.

sanjay: SRE concern: fallback behavior matters. If client doesn't send negotiation header, will they keep getting the legacy envelope? what's the behavior during the soft-deprecation window? we need alerts for traffic spikes when clients start defaulting to newer variants.

alex: Current proposal:
- If no `Accept-Response-Envelope` header: continue returning legacy envelope during soft-deprecation.
- During hard enforcement, requests without the header get 426 / 406-style response (client must opt-in).
- Pinning header: `X-Redwood-Model-Pin: model-name@v2` (optional).

Example headers we plan to document:
```
X-Redwood-Model-Pin: rw-base-small@2026-01-12
Accept-Response-Envelope: v2
X-Redwood-Client-Version: 1.4.0
```

maria: Nice. Can we also emit a structured deprecation warning in the response body during soft-deprecation? e.g., a `warnings` array in `meta` for clients that parse bodies. That way both header-less and header'd clients see a signal.

alex: Yes — we can add `meta.warnings` during soft-dep. It won't be present in legacy envelope, so for headerless clients we add a small `warnings` JSON payload outside the main envelope to avoid breaking. We'll spec the exact shape in the doc.

jordan: Docs + SDK plan: publish migration guide, example patches for JS/Python SDKs, and add runtime telemetry samples. Product will prepare customer comms and a blog post at announce + two reminder emails during the 90d window.

sanjay: Rollout thought: recommend canaries by customer segment, not just percent. e.g., internal + partners (1%), low-risk accounts (10%), then broader. Suggested cadence: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over ~2 weeks per stage, with automatic rollback on error thresholds (error rate + latency + increased timeouts).

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary-step-1 (1%) triggered by eng-platform at 2026-03-17T15:12:00Z

maria: Action items: @alex write the header contract + sample responses by EOD Friday; @jordan own the customer comms timeline; @sanjay define SLO thresholds and rollback rules. I'll draft the migration checklist for SDK owners.

alex: Ack — I'll drop the header spec into the PR and link to a short json schema for `meta`.

jordan: I'll schedule the comms and loop in account-exec for the top 20 customers.

sanjay: I'll add canary alerts to the playbook and create a runbook snippet for the common failure modes.

maria: One more: what's our recommended default for the `X-Redwood-Model-Pin` if customers do nothing? do we map to a pinned alias or to "legacy-default"? Need to be explicit in docs.

alex: Recommend mapping to `legacy-default` by name for now. That gives us a clear knob to flip later and makes logs simpler. We'll include examples: `X-Redwood-Model-Pin: legacy-default` and `X-Redwood-Model-Pin: rw-base-small@2026-01-12`.

maria: Great. Closing the loop here — thanks all. Please ping this thread when the PR + doc links are ready. :thumbsup:
